findings.text: follow-on (nit): the success-path return contradicts the function's own docstring. llm_health_check_with_decisions binds `healthy, detail = llm_health_check(section)` at line 462, then rebinds `healthy, detail = decisions_health_check(service)` at line 464, and returns `True, detail` at line 466 — so on the all-healthy path the detail is the DECISIONS route host, not the chat seat's. The docstring at line 453 promises 'and the seat's detail when both succeed', and the evidence fragment says nothing about the success label. TRIGGERING INPUT: with llm_health_check stubbed to (True,'98dci4-gpu-0003:18802') and decisions_health_check to (True,'openrouter.ai'), llm_health_check_with_decisions('discovery-score') returns (True,'openrouter.ai') — verified in this reviewer's worktree. Effect is display-only: the panel's llm row shows 'openrouter.ai' where the single-seat check showed the score seat's host. The composed test test_healthy_when_both_reachable asserts only `detail` truthiness, so it does not pin either meaning. Fix is one word — return the seat's stored detail — or one docstring correction.

follow-on (coverage note, not a defect): the probe is built from DECISIONS_ENDPOINT's origin only — `probe_url = f"{origin.scheme}://{origin.netloc}/api/v1/key"` at line 417 — so it exercises the OpenRouter origin's key-info endpoint and the facility-discovery credential, not the decisions path itself (/api/alpha/decisions). A deployment in which the alpha decisions route were removed or rerouted while openrouter.ai/api/v1/key stayed up would read llm up. This is the cheap, zero-cost reachability probe the node's spec explicitly allowed ('an authenticated request that costs nothing, or the API's models listing'), and it is strictly better than the prior check, which probed the LiteLLM proxy every code-discovery call bypasses. Recorded so the coverage boundary is on the record, not as work this node should have done differently. Positive control: the live probe returns (True, 'openrouter.ai') in this reviewer's session.

justifications.durability: The change is the durable shape for its scope. The probe derives its URL from DECISIONS_ENDPOINT rather than a literal, so a host move is followed; it resolves the credential through get_api_key_for_service(service) with the same 'facility-discovery' tag the relevance calls use, so the probe and the calls can never drift onto different keys; it reuses _service_headers rather than rebuilding the X-Title/Referer block; and it distinguishes the failure modes (endpoint refused / endpoint timeout / auth refused (401|403) / HTTP n) so the panel names a cause rather than a bare down. The panel stays fail-closed but non-critical (critical=False), matching the single-seat check it replaces, so a decisions outage does not pause workers. Deductions: the docstring's success-path promise is not what the code returns (services.py:453 vs :466), and the probe validates origin reachability plus credential, not the decisions alpha path specifically (services.py:417). Neither changes behaviour on the named measure.
justifications.evidence: Strong and independently reproduced. I re-ran the full gate at the reviewed head 11a270c (3 failed, 1495 passed, EXIT=1, 171.58s) matching the reviewed record exactly. I reproduced the declared negative control independently, against the reviewed source with the decisions probe mutated to always report healthy: llm_health_check_with_decisions('discovery-score') returns healthy True and the guard fails 'assert True is False', EXIT=1 — the same first assertion the node's negative-control.log records. I confirmed the three failures are pre-existing by running the same three ids in my own unmodified worktree, where they fail identically (3 failed, EXIT=1). I ran the live probe as a positive control and it returns (True, 'openrouter.ai'), so the mocked-only tests are probing a URL that answers. Deductions: the base arm (base-arm.log) ran only the three failing ids rather than a full base suite, so it establishes 'these three fail at base' but yields no base pass count; and the composed function's tests assert only `detail` truthiness, so the success-label mismatch is untested.
justifications.fit: The additions follow the module's own idiom: function-local urllib imports, a 10 s timeout, an (healthy, detail) tuple, no plan/sprint/ticket label in a symbol, comment or commit, and no AI attribution (a case-insensitive scan of both commit bodies returns 0 hits). The CLI change reuses the existing extra_service_checks mechanism that imas_codex/cli/sn.py already uses rather than inventing a bespoke monitor wiring, and it preserves the prior llm row's poll interval and critical flag. Deduction: the docstring at services.py:453 states a success-path behaviour the body does not implement.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §25's second-wave bullet is met: the code status panel's llm row now reflects both the local score seat and the decisions route, and names which endpoint is unreachable. decisions_health_check sends one authenticated GET to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key (origin parsed from DECISIONS_ENDPOINT) with the facility-discovery credential and no model/state/questions, so no decision is billed — verified live as (True, 'openrouter.ai'); llm_health_check_with_decisions returns 'score (...)' when the seat is down and 'decisions (...)' when the route is down, verified by the new tests; and code.py registers the composed check as the llm row with check_model=False so the single-seat check is not duplicated. The node kept the name, 60 s interval and non-critical gating. One deduction: on the all-healthy path the row reports the decisions host rather than the score seat's, contradicting the function's docstring — a display-level mismatch, not a failure of the named measure.
justifications.reuse: Good. The probe reuses get_api_key_for_service, _service_headers and the DECISIONS_ENDPOINT constant rather than duplicating the credential and header logic the decisions call layer owns, and it composes the existing llm_health_check instead of reimplementing the chat-seat probe; the CLI reuses DiscoveryConfig.extra_service_checks and ServiceMonitor.add_check rather than a new monitor path. No new dependency was introduced and no second mechanism was added beside the existing ones.
